text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.98% today to $129.34, recovering slightly from a steep four-day slide that wiped out 5.6% of its value since mid-September. The modest gain came as oil prices stabilized—U.S. crude held at $96.41 per barrel—after a volatile week driven by shifting geopolitical risk. A Senate vote against ending the Iran war and reports of potential talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (a critical shipping chokepoint for global oil) created conflicting signals: war risk staying elevated, but also hints that supply disruption might ease, which pulled oil prices back from session highs.

The bigger story behind the recent selloff is the underlying price collapse in oil itself. The stock's 5.6% drop over two weeks tracks directly with crude falling from higher levels earlier in the month. Separately, the industry is pushing back hard against a potential Trump diesel export ban—diesel is now at $6.51 per gallon, nearly triple last year's level—which creates political noise but also signals tight refining conditions that could support margins if policy doesn't shift sharply.
